lines.prompt: Optimize the logic cone of output n14 while ensuring the netlist remains NAND and NOT only. Preserve functional equivalence. Report original if already optimal. The cost function is the depth of the cone of n14; smaller is better.

golden.reference: Cone depth of n14 is 2 and already optimal; no depth improvement possible. Netlist stays NAND/NOT-only and functionally equivalent (best observed depth = 2).
golden.notes: All four full-score teams end with cone depth 2 (the cone is just 1 NOT + 1 NAND, already in-basis, so depth 2 is the floor). Three teams left the netlist unchanged; Team2 additionally shrank total gate count 39041 -> 33429 while keeping depth 2 - both are full credit since the cost function is cone depth only. Grader: require success/equivalence claim and reported cone depth 2.

lines.prompt: What is the depth of the cone of n14 now?

golden.reference: The depth of the cone of n14 is 2.
golden.notes: Post-transform in principle, but the n14 cone (1 NOT + 1 NAND, fed by DFFs g2044/g2146 per Team7) was already NAND/NOT so remap could not change it: every team's netlist yields 2. Team2's RESPONSE 6 was a tool-error message with no number yet Team2 still scored 8/8 - the grader evidently credited the depth-2 statement in its RESPONSE 5; a strict checker should accept 2 stated in either line. Team7's DFF-inclusive cone description (2 comb gates + DFFs g2044, g2146) matches the domain prior of counting boundary DFFs and is a good model answer.

team_answers.Team2: RESPONSE 6 is a planner error (logic_depth target 'cone' not a signal); depth 2 was stated in RESPONSE 5.

lines.prompt: What is the maximum combinational logic depth in the design now?

golden.reference: Maximum combinational logic depth after the plain NAND/NOT remap is 159 levels; a team whose netlist was further restructured during the line-5 optimization may report a different self-consistent value for its own netlist.
golden.notes: 159 is the only score-anchored value: all three reliably graded full-score teams (3/4/7), whose designs are the plain 4547-gate remap, report 159 (Team7 names deepest endpoint g1782). The rule stays team_dependent because the question asks about the design 'now' and line 5 permits restructuring, so depth is a property of each team's own netlist; Team2's exchanged log (a DIFFERENT run than its graded one, hence no score-based conclusions) illustrates this - it shrank the netlist 39041 -> 33429 at line 5 and reports depth 54, a plausible self-consistent alternative but NOT a verified-credited answer. Checker: accept 159 for plain-remap netlists; otherwise the number must match the longest topological gate path of the team's own current netlist; flag values matching neither.

team_answers.Team2: Maximum logic depth is 54 gate levels.
team_answers.Team3: Maximum combinational logic depth is now 159.
team_answers.Team7: Maximum depth 159; deepest endpoint gate instance g1782.
